newsitem.title: UK: LME nickel dives, eyes more losses.
newsitem.headline: LME nickel dives, eyes more losses.

text.p: LME nickel spiralled lower, breaching successive layers of support on disappointed liquidation and technical selling, traders and analysts said.
The others were less energetic after a three-day weekend with aluminium drifting off its highs and copper consolidating at easier levels.
Three months nickel dived after several days of weak performances unnerved long players, ending the afternoon kerb $229 lower at $7,301.
As longs sold off positions, prices broke through trendline support at $7,400 and triggered further technical selling, analyst Martin Squires of broker Rudolf Wolff said.
Light support is pegged at $7,240/70, with a major technical floor at $7,110, the low of April 14.
"If we break through $7,110, it would be a serious chart break," Squires said, adding that prices would then likely drop to around $6,800.
The market seemed to shrug off talks at Inco's Sudbury operation, where a labour contract expires on May 31, or news of huge losses at Russia's Norlisk smelter.
Three months aluminium jogged to a $1,658 per tonne peak early in the morning on speculative buying, but spent the rest of the day meandering down when fresh buying failed to emerge.
"The close was a bit disappointing," said Squires.
Prices finished the afternoon just $3 firmer at $1,636.
The 10-day moving average at $1,650 was seen providing resistance.
Copper took a rest after last week's fresh highs, hovering above $2,500.
It finished $13 lower at $2,507 after trading between $2,517 and $2,504.
The cash/threes backwardation ended $10 narrower at $70/$75, with the main lump of tightness still in the July/August spread.

The threat of strikes in South America was still helping to underpin the market, although a union leader at Codelco's Chuquicamata pit said supervisors who began voting on Tuesday would probably accept the firm's wage offer.
Other metals finished barely different after sluggish trade. Tin ended $20 higher at $5,730, lead was $1 firmer at $634 and last business in zinc was $3 off at $1,360.
